newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa gold sales underreported by 25 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa gold sales underreported by 25 pct - paper.

text.p: South African gold sales were underreported by 25 percent last year after the Central Statistical Service was fed incorrect information by the Minerals Bureau, the Business Day newspaper said on Thursday.
The CSS figure for total gold sales in 1996 was 21.2 billion rand, but this excluded toll refining at the Rand Refinery, which is owned by the major mining companies.
According to the Chamber of Mines, gold sales were 26.5 billion rand, based on total production -- including non-chamber members -- multiplied by the Reserve Bank's average monthly gold price.

The underreporting could mean that GDP figures for last year are too low. It could also mean that the country actually had a surplus on its current account in the fourth quarter of 1996 rather than the small reported deficit of 50 million rand.
